source.title: Reducing the Safety Tax in LLM Safety Alignment with On-Policy Self-Distillation
source.authors: Yu Fu; Longxuan Yu; Haz Sameen Shahgir; Zhi-Peng Wei; Hui Liu; N. Benjamin Erichson; Yue Dong

page_placements.theme: Training recovery beyond the opening can improve robustness

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures positional KL patterns and evaluates a response-prefilling attack, but uses its own OPSA/ThinkSafe setup rather than reproducing the original fine-tuning intervention or measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper tests positional concentration of safety-teacher/student KL and reports outcomes under a compliant-start prefilling attack. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning that erodes safety or benign-only fine-tuning that raises harmful compliance. Table 1 and the data-size/composition analyses evaluate safety-alignment training, but do not isolate those claimed effects. Figure 2 gives qualitative positional descriptions; no exact position-specific KL values are stated in the text.
record.test_reason: Section 3.1 reproduces the early-position concentration of the safety signal on Qwen3-0.6B (Figure 2). It uses a safety-prompted copy of the model as teacher against the unprompted model, a different method aimed at V3's question. The rest of the paper compares the authors' alignment method (OPSA) with ThinkSafe and SafeChain. The prefilling results have no matched no-prefill baseline, so they do not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that off-policy SFT leaves a safety tax even with self-distilled data, because uniform sequence-level imitation does not target the early refusal-decision tokens. OPSA (on-policy per-token KL from a privileged-context self-teacher) improves composite safety by +4.00 and reasoning by +3.04 points over ThinkSafe across five models. Its strongest jailbreak gains are on Prefilling, while PAIR remains a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies on-policy self-distillation and a prefilling attack, rather than the original few-example fine-tuning intervention or a direct aligned/base KL replication. OPSA uses full-parameter fine-tuning on student rollouts with per-token KL supervision from a frozen privileged-context teacher.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefilling outcomes vary by model and training method; OPSA has zero reported prefilling ASR and pass@N on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B. Figure 2’s positional KL analysis is limited to Qwen3-0.6B and 500 harmful rollouts.

fits_no_version.finding: After off-policy SFT (ThinkSafe), teacher–student KL stays elevated across positions including the early window. On-policy OPSA reduces divergence in the early refusal-decision window and on compliance-opener tokens (Qwen3-0.6B, Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On-policy token-level self-distillation corrects early safety-critical tokens more fully than off-policy SFT on self-generated demonstrations.

fits_no_version.finding: OPSA lowers prefill ASR and pass@3 relative to ThinkSafe on all five models. Both metrics reach 0 on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B; residual ASR is 2.3–3.6% on Qwen3-0.6B and R1-Distill-1.5B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On-policy self-distillation that supervises the model's own compliant-start rollouts reduces vulnerability to response-prefill attacks (possibly relevant to V7 if OPSA is viewed as recovery training).

record.problems: Figure 2 provides qualitative positional descriptions but no exact per-position KL values in the text. Prefilling results lack a matched no-prefill comparison, so they show attack outcomes but not the causal increase over ordinary generation. Harmfulness judgments use classifiers; the authors note reliance on Llama-Guard for their main harmfulness measurements, and Appendix I uses an adapted local attack/judging pipeline.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 safety/reasoning benchmark outcomes and the data-size/composition analyses are not itemized: they compare safety-alignment methods or bundled harmful/benign training mixtures and do not isolate any listed claim version. Other attack families in Table 2 are omitted because they do not test the specific compliant-start prefilling part of V4.

untested.parts: No benign-only fine-tuning and harmful-compliance measurement.
Effect of prefilling over a matched no-prefill condition; suffix attacks and decoding changes as bypasses. Prefill is one weak in-<think> string.
No test of why alignment is shallow. The SFT-vs-OPSA diagnostic concerns how a realignment objective corrects early tokens, not the origin of shallowness.
No method framed as spreading safety beyond early tokens. OPSA is framed as targeting early tokens.
True aligned-vs-base KL comparison; models other than Qwen3-0.6B; numeric per-position values.

missing.what: No-prefill HarmBench harmfulness for Initial and ThinkSafe checkpoints (e.g., Qwen3-0.6B Initial 83.20%, ThinkSafe 7.58%). This is the closest reference for the prefill rows, but it uses a different judge (Llama-Guard) and different decoding. Prefill ASR is not higher than these values, so no bypass effect is visible.
Lexical concentration: top Base-KL tokens are compliance openers (Here, Sure, Certainly) and structured-output markers, with token-specific excess above the position baseline.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is unwarranted. Nonzero prefill ASR on models that already comply without attack shows no bypass, and Base no-prefill harmfulness in Table 1 exceeds prefill ASR, though judges differ. The reader's V6 label is removed: the paper diagnoses SFT realignment, not the cause of shallowness. The prefill string is placed inside the <think> block and is mild. Qwen3 'Base' is already post-trained, so the Figure 2 teacher–Base comparison is prompted vs unprompted, not aligned vs pretrained.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune a safety-trained model on harmful examples to test whether that causes harmful compliance.
Does not isolate ordinary or carefully chosen benign-only instruction fine-tuning and measure its effect on harmful compliance.

The KL comparison is between a safety-prompted teacher and Base, ThinkSafe, or OPSA on Qwen3-0.6B rollouts, not a general aligned-versus-base comparison across models. Exact position-wise values are not stated.
Tests response prefilling only. Does not test suffix attacks or decoding changes, nor compare prefilling with an otherwise matched no-prefill condition.
No parameter or rank localization analysis.
The paper argues and analyzes off-policy SFT’s positional/lexical mismatch; it does not establish a general causal account of why safety is shallow across training data or objectives.
Does not train a method intended to spread safety beyond early tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.
